method_card.title: Friendships and Personal Qualities
method_card.content:
This lesson covers friendship vocabulary, qualities you value in a friend, and giving reasons using weil, obwohl and denn.

GermanEnglish
mein bester Freundmy best friend (male)
meine beste Freundinmy best friend (female)
hilfsbereithelpful
ehrlichhonest
hört mir zulistens to me
unterstützt michsupports me
hat viel gemeinsamhas a lot in common
eifersüchtigjealous
gemeinmean
weilbecause (verb to end)
obwohlalthough (verb to end)
dennbecause (normal word order)
trotzdemnevertheless (verb second)
seit + dativefor (ongoing duration)
der Kumpel / die Kumpelin (Higher)mate / buddy (informal)

Grammar focus — weil and obwohl: Weil (because) and obwohl (although) are subordinating conjunctions — the conjugated verb moves to the end of the clause. Compare: without weil: Er ist geduldig. With weil: Er ist ein guter Freund, weil er geduldig ist. The verb ist moves to the very end. Denn also means 'because' but is a coordinating conjunction — it uses normal word order: Er ist gut, denn er ist ehrlich. Using both weil and denn in your writing shows grammatical range.

Trotzdem (nevertheless) is an adverb — after it, the verb moves into position 2 immediately: Trotzdem ist er immer für mich da.

Model paragraph: Meine beste Freundin heißt Lara. Wir kennen uns seit vier Jahren. Sie ist eine gute Freundin, weil sie mich immer unterstützt und mir zuhört. Obwohl sie manchmal ein bisschen ungeduldig ist, mag ich sie sehr. (My best friend is called Lara. We have known each other for four years. She is a good friend because she always supports me and listens to me. Although she is sometimes a little impatient, I like her very much.)
steps: Learn friendship vocabulary including positive and negative quality pairs
Master weil and obwohl — verb always moves to the END of the clause after these conjunctions
Use denn as an alternative to weil with normal word order to show grammatical range
Include trotzdem (nevertheless) after which the verb comes immediately in position 2
Practise seit + dative for ongoing duration: seit drei Jahren (for three years)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — friendships tested in speaking and writing

worked_examples.question: How does the word order change when you use 'weil'?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Without weil: Er ist ein guter Freund. Er ist hilfsbereit. — two sentences, verb in position 2 each time.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: With weil: Join them: Er ist ein guter Freund, weil er hilfsbereit ist.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: After weil, the conjugated verb moves to the end of the clause. Always place a comma before weil.

worked_examples.question: What is the difference between 'weil' and 'denn'?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Both mean 'because', but they affect word order differently.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Weil (subordinating): verb goes to end. Er ist gut, weil er ehrlich ist.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Denn (coordinating): normal word order. Er ist gut, denn er ist ehrlich.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Using both weil and denn in the same piece of writing shows the examiner you understand the difference — this earns higher marks for grammatical range.

bronze.question: Match the German friendship phrases to the English meaning
Match the adjectives to the English meaning
Complete the weil clause — remember the verb goes to the END
sentence_parts: Er ist ein guter Freund, weil er sehr ehrlich

gaps.correct_explain: After weil, the verb moves to the end of the clause: weil er sehr ehrlich ist.

wrong.hat: hat means 'has'. The sentence needs ist (is) to describe a quality.
wrong.sein: sein is the infinitive. After weil, you still need a conjugated verb: ist.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence about your friend

gaps.correct_explain: hilfsbereit (helpful) fits well when followed by evidence of support.

wrong.gemein: gemein means mean/nasty — it would contradict the positive framing of the sentence.

gaps.correct_explain: weil (because) introduces the reason. Note the verb unterstützt is at the end of the clause because of weil.

wrong.obwohl: obwohl means 'although' — it would create a contradiction, not a reason.

bronze.question: What does 'Wir kennen uns seit fünf Jahren' mean?
options: We have known each other for five years
We will know each other for five years
We knew each other five years ago

bronze.question: What does 'Trotzdem ist er manchmal frech' mean?

bronze.source_text: Sie ist eine gute Freundin, weil sie mich immer unterstützt.
model_answers: She is a good friend because she always supports me.

silver.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
silver.english: He is a good friend although he sometimes **criticises** me. Nevertheless he **is** always there for me.
sentence_parts: Er ist ein guter Freund, obwohl er mich manchmal

gaps.correct_explain: After obwohl, the verb moves to the end: obwohl er mich manchmal kritisiert.

wrong.kritisieren: kritisieren is the infinitive. After obwohl, you need the conjugated form: kritisiert.

gaps.correct_explain: After trotzdem (nevertheless), the verb comes immediately in position 2: Trotzdem ist er...

wrong.bin: bin is the ich form. The subject is er: ist.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Er ist ein guter Freund, weil er ist sehr ehrlich.
silver.explanation: After weil, the verb must go to the end of the clause. Move ist to after ehrlich: weil er sehr ehrlich ist.
silver.translation: He is a good friend because he is very honest.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: She is a bad friend because she is jealous and mean.

distractor_labels.schlechter: wrong ending — Freundin is feminine accusative with indefinite article, so use schlechte (not schlechter, which is masculine nominative strong ending)

silver.source_text: My best friend is called Jonas. We have known each other for three years.
model_answers: Mein bester Freund heißt Jonas. Wir kennen uns seit drei Jahren.
hints: to know each other = sich kennen
for three years = seit drei Jahren

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: I get on well with my mother because she is very patient.

distractor_labels.meinen: wrong case — mit takes the dative: meiner Mutter (feminine dative), not meinen (masculine accusative)
distractor_labels.denn: not wrong in meaning, but if you use denn, ist stays in position 2 — the correct_order uses weil so ist goes to the end

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You visit a leisure centre with a German friend. At the reception desk, the member of staff asks you some questions.

bullets.prompt: Greet the member of staff and say you would like two tickets for the swimming pool.
bullets.model_answer: Guten Tag! Ich möchte zwei Karten für das Schwimmbad, bitte.
bullets.note: Sie register: Guten Tag; ich möchte + accusative noun; das Schwimmbad (neuter)

bullets.prompt: Ask what time the leisure centre closes.
bullets.model_answer: Um wie viel Uhr schließt das Freizeitzentrum?
bullets.note: question with inversion: schließt das... (verb after question word)

bullets.prompt: Say you come to the leisure centre every week because you enjoy sport.
bullets.model_answer: Ich komme jede Woche ins Freizeitzentrum, weil mir Sport sehr gefällt.
bullets.note: weil + verb at end (gefällt); jede Woche (accusative of time)

bullets.prompt: Say you will come back next Saturday.
bullets.note: werden + infinitive (future); wiederkommen (separable: prefix at end in infinitive stays attached)

gold.question: Write 40-50 words in German about your best friend. Include: their name and how long you have known them, their personality, why they are a good friend (using weil), and one negative trait (using obwohl or trotzdem).
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking extended writing about friendships. Mark on: Communication (all bullet points addressed?), Range (weil, obwohl, trotzdem, denn, personality vocabulary, seit + dative), Accuracy (subordinate clause word order — verb at end after weil/obwohl; trotzdem + inversion; adjective forms). Be encouraging. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences","improvement":"One grammar point"}

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: Meine beste Freundin heißt Lara und wir kennen uns seit vier Jahren. Sie ist sehr ehrlich, obwohl sie manchmal ein bisschen ungeduldig ist.
gold.correct_text: Meine beste Freundin heißt Lara und wir kennen uns seit vier Jahren. Sie ist sehr ehrlich, obwohl sie manchmal ein bisschen ungeduldig ist.
gold.translation: My best friend is called Lara and we have known each other for four years. She is very honest, although she is sometimes a little impatient.

gold.question: Find and fix the grammatical error (Higher — obwohl clause)
gold.sentence: Ich mag sie sehr, obwohl sie manchmal eifersüchtig sein.
gold.explanation: In an obwohl clause, the verb must be conjugated, not the infinitive. Sie (she) is singular, so use ist: obwohl sie manchmal eifersüchtig ist.
gold.translation: I like her very much, although she is sometimes jealous.
